faq.question: Is a Master’s in Biomedical Engineering available in Mauritius?
faq.answer: A dedicated Master’s in Biomedical Engineering is not listed in the University of Mauritius’s reviewed 2026–2027 postgraduate catalogue. Related programmes include the Master of Public Health and MSc Microbiology, but they have different academic objectives.

faq.question: Which university can I contact for related programmes?
faq.answer: The University of Mauritius is a starting point for exploring health and science-related postgraduate options. Ask the university directly about biomedical engineering research opportunities and whether any suitable programme is planned for a future intake.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Mauritius as a student?
faq.answer: An indicative budget is MUR 15,000–25,000 per month, approximately ₹30,000–₹50,000 using the exchange rate assumed in this article. Actual expenses depend on accommodation and lifestyle.

faq.question: Can Indian students apply for related postgraduate programmes in Mauritius?
faq.answer: Indian applicants can enquire about international admission, but eligibility, qualification recognition, fees and study-permit requirements depend on the selected institution and programme.

faq.question: What career options are available after studying biomedical engineering?
faq.answer: Depending on your qualification and experience, possible areas include medical device development, biomedical research, medical equipment services, quality assurance and healthcare technology management. Choose a course that provides the technical training required for your target role.
